dataset: IBM Transactions for Anti Money Laundering (AML)
classification: A selected and pseudonymized subset is Enhanced Data, not an unrestricted Result.
scope_requested: One review period of the alert store, carried whole, with each alert's pseudonymized subject, its computed trigger quantities, a bounded sample of its contributing transactions, its position under each baseline ordering and under the learned ranker, and its simulated outcome.
why_a_separate_decision: The approved replay decision covers bounded replay artifacts of 55 transactions across six cases. The triage slice is a different and much larger selection, and an approval granted for one scope never carries over to another.
publication_conditions: Carry a prominent modification, selection, and pseudonymization notice.
Retain IBM / Erik Altman attribution and source hyperlink.
Provide the CDLA-Sharing-1.0 text or a reliable hyperlink.
Admit only an artifact reproduced from a verified local source manifest.
Publish computed trigger quantities only; the tuned rule parameter values stay private and are described by name, unit and direction of effect.

owner_approval.scope: One review period of the Signal Ledger triage artifact, derived from the exact verified HI-Small v8 source checksum only, under the publication conditions recorded above. This approval does not extend to any other period, to the LI-Small variant, to the alert store, to the feature table, or to the tuned rule parameter values.

supersedes.reason: That approval covered a slice built by rules engine version 1. The engine was rebuilt as version 2, widening the fan rules to a three period counterparty window, which changes the alert population the slice is drawn from. The source file, its checksum, the variant and the review period are unchanged, and so are the publication conditions. A slice drawn from a different alert population is a different slice, so it is approved explicitly rather than carried across.
